lessons.goal: 依觀察單位判斷數量，區分目擊次數與不同個體。

questions.evidence: For an observation lesson, a teacher places eight model birds around a garden and asks two groups to count them from different paths. Group A records six sightings, and Group B records five. A student adds the numbers and announces eleven birds.
options: Six.
Five.
Eight.
Eleven.
questions.prompt: How many sightings did Group A record?

questions.evidence: The teacher asks whether the groups might have seen some of the same models. Each bird carries a small colored tag. Comparing notes shows that three tagged birds appear in both lists. The class combines the lists and counts each tag only once.
questions.explanation: 每隻模型有可核對的色標。
options: Colored tags.
The number of garden paths alone.
A rule that no models can be seen twice.
The students' shoe colors.

questions.evidence:
For an observation lesson, a teacher places eight model birds around a garden and asks two groups to count them from different paths. Group A records six sightings, and Group B records five. A student adds the numbers and announces eleven birds.

The teacher asks whether the groups might have seen some of the same models. Each bird carries a small colored tag. Comparing notes shows that three tagged birds appear in both lists. The class combines the lists and counts each tag only once.

The total is eight different models, although there were eleven recorded sightings. The teacher keeps both numbers and labels them clearly. One describes observations; the other describes distinct objects. Before a later outdoor survey, students discuss how much harder it would be to recognize untagged moving birds. The model activity gives them a counting question to consider, not a guarantee that real field observations will be equally simple.
